US stock indices are mixed today, with the Dow Jones Industrials falling to a 5.25-month low. Market sentiment took a hit today as chipmakers and AI-infrastructure stocks weakened after Nvidia erased an overnight rally and fell more than -1% despite a stellar Q3 earnings report. Nvidia initially rallied more than +3% in overnight trade as market concerns about the durability of the artificial intelligence trade eased after the company reported blowout Q3 earnings and raised its revenue growth target for 2028. Weakness in energy producers, mining stocks, and health insurers is also weighing on the overall market today.

Today's -2% fall in WTI crude oil to a 2.75-month low has lowered inflation expectations and is supportive for stocks. The 10-year T-note yield is down -4 bp to 5.07%. Also, the recent disruptions to air travel, banking, and other services are boosting demand for cybersecurity stocks.

Strong demand is seen for Anthropic's IPO, set to price later today. The company is marketing 825 million shares in aggregate for $70 to $78 each and is expected to price at the top of the range. According to people familiar with the matter, the IPO is close to seven times oversubscribed.

US housing news is mixed today. Oct housing starts rose +9.9% m/m to 1.309 million, stronger than expectations of 1.250 million. However, Oct building permits, a proxy for future construction, fell -7.4% to a 6.5-year low of 1.295 million, weaker than expectations of 1.375 million. Also, Oct pending home sales fell -4.7% m/m, weaker than expectations of -2.0% m/m.

US MBA mortgage applications fell -2.3% in the week ended November 13, with purchase mortgage applications down -2.5% and refinancing mortgage applications down -1.5%. The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose +14 bp to 7.35% from 7.21% in the prior week.

Hawkish comments today from Fed Governor Christopher Waller are bearish for stocks and bonds, as he said inflation is headed in the wrong direction and "we have to be a little more aggressive in our rate hikes to try to get inflation down," urging the Fed to consider a 50 bp interest rate increase at next month's FOMC meeting.

Dec WTI crude oil prices (CLZ26) is down more than -2% today at a 2.75-month low today on signs of larger global oil supplies. Iraq said it restarted crude oil flows through a pipeline connecting the main northern oil fields of Kirkuk with the port of Ceyhan in Turkey after a 12-year halt. Iraq began pumping crude into the pipeline at a rate of 120,000 bpd, with plans to boost the volume to 500,000 bpd. Crude prices are also under pressure on hopes that diplomacy can end the US-Iran war after Iran's semi-official Iranian Students' News Agency said Iran is "seriously pursuing an exit from the neither war nor peace situation through dignified diplomacy."

Stocks are supported by the prospect of solid quarterly earnings. According to data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence, Q3 S&P 500 earnings are expected to climb by +31% from a year earlier, up from a July estimate of 22%. As of today, 461 of the S&P 500 companies have reported results, with 84% beating estimates.

Overseas stock markets are mixed today. The Euro Stoxx 50 fell to a 1-week low and is down -0.53%. China's Shanghai Composite recovered from a 1.25-year low and closed up +0.09%. Japan's Nikkei-225 Stock Average rebounded from a 1-week low and closed up +0.28%.

Interest Rates

December 10-year T-notes (ZNZ6) are up +6 ticks today. The 10-year T-note yield is down -3.8 bp to 5.068%. T-notes are moving higher as today's -2% fall in WTI crude oil to a 2.75-month low has reduced inflation expectations. Also, today's larger-than-expected decline in US Oct building permits to a 6.5-year low is dovish for Fed policy.

T-note gains are limited today as strength in stocks has curbed safe-haven demand for government debt securities. Also, hawkish comments today from Fed Governor Christopher Waller weighed on T-notes when he said inflation is headed in the wrong direction and the Fed should consider a 50 bp rate hike at the December FOMC meeting. In addition, supply pressures are bearish for T-notes as the Treasury will auction $16 billion of 20-year T-bonds later today.

The markets are now pricing in a 100% chance of a +25 bp rate hike at the FOMC's next meeting on December 8-9.

European government bond yields are moving lower today. The 10-year German bund yield fell from a 3.5-week high of 3.401% and is down -0.1 bp to 3.374%. The 10-year UK gilt yield is down -6.8 bp to 5.302%.

Eurozone Oct CPI was left unrevised at +4.0% y/y. However, Oct core CPI was revised upward by +0.1 to 2.6% y/y from the previously reported +2.5% y/y.

UK Oct CPI rose +3.6% y/y, right on expectations and the largest pace of increase in a year. Oct core CPI was unchanged from Sep at +2.8% y/y, right on expectations.

The markets are now pricing in a 95% chance of a +25 bp rate hike at the ECB's next policy meeting on December 17.

US Stock Movers

Chipmakers and AI-infrastructure stocks are under pressure today after Nvidia (NVDA) erased overnight gains and slid more than -1% despite reporting Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, well above the consensus of $109.33 billion, and raising its 2028 revenue growth estimate to up 75% from an August forecast of 70%. Sandisk (SNDK) is down more than -3%, and Qualcomm (QCOM) is down more than -2%. Also, Marvell Technology (MRVL), Micron Technology (MU), and Intel (INTC) are down more than -1%.

Mining stocks are falling today after gold and silver prices tumbled to 13.5-month lows and copper slid to a 4.75-month low. Anglogold Ashanti (AU) is down more than -8%, and Freeport McMoRan (FCX) is down more than -7% to lead losers in the S&P 500. Also, Newmont Corp (NEM) and Barrick Mining (B) are down more than -7%, and Coeur Mining (CDE), Hecla Mining (HL) and Southern Copper (SCCO) are down more than -6%.

Energy producers and service providers are falling today, with WTI crude oil down more than -1% to a 2.75-month low. Valero Energy (VLO) is down more than -5%, and Marathon Petroleum (MPC) and Phillips 66 (PSX) are down more than -4%. Also, Chevron (CVX) and Occidental Petroleum (OXY) are down more than -3%, and ConocoPhillips (COP) and ExxonMobil Holdings (XOM) are down more than -2%. In addition, APA Corp (APA), Devon Energy (DVN) and Halliburton (HAL) are down more than -1%.

Health insurance stocks are under pressure for a second day today after the US government proposed a Medicare Advantage audit framework in its CRUSH proposal that analysts view as negative for the group. Humana (HUM) is down more than -6%, and UnitedHealth Group (UNH) is down more than -6% to lead losers in the Dow Jones Industrials. Also, Molina Healthcare (MOH) and Centene (CNC) are down more than -5%, and Elevance Health (ELV) is down more than -4%. In addition, CVS Health (CVS) is down more than -3%, the Cigna Group (CI) and HCA Holdings (HCA) are down more than -2%, and United Health Services (UHS) is down more than -1%.

Cybersecurity stocks are rallying today. SentinelOne (S) is up more than +8%, and Crowdstrike Holdings (CRWD), Palo Alto Networks (PANW), and Okta (OKTA) are up more than +6%. Also, Zscaler (ZS), Cloudflare (NET), and Fortinet (FTNT) are up more than +4%, and Gen Digital (GEN) is up more than +2%.

TJX Cos (TJX) is up more than +7% to lead gainers in the S&P 500 after reporting Q3 net sales of $16.0 billion, better than the consensus of $15.84 billion.

Tandem Diabetes Care (TNDM) is up more than +6% after Stifel upgraded the stock to buy from hold with a price target of $26.

Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) is up more than +5% to lead gainers in the Nasdaq 100 on several positive reviews for the company's Grand Theft Auto VI game, which is set to launch on Thursday.

Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) is down more than -11% after announcing it plans to offer $550 million in common stock under an equity distribution agreement.

Dolby Laboratories (DLB) is down more than -2% after forecasting 2027 adjusted EPS of $4.27 to $4.42, weaker than the consensus of $4.58.

Credit: Spencer Platt / Getty Images

Stock futures suggest the Nasdaq and S&P 500 are likely to rise; Nvidia shares are rising after it handed in strong results late Tuesday; Anthropic is expected to finalize IPO share prices today; Target and Lowe's shares are falling during a busy period for retail results; and investors await minutes from the Federal Reserve's last policy meeting.

Here's what to know today:

Stock Futures Point to (Mostly) Higher Open

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 appear poised to bounce back from Tuesday's losses, which came amid anxiety ahead of Nvidia's results. Futures tied to the Nasdaq 100 were recently up 0.6% and futures tied to the S&P 500 were up 0.2%, while those associated with the Dow were down marginally. AI-related stocks were on the rise after Nvidia handed in strong numbers last night (more on that below). Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), Micron (MU) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) were recently up about 2%.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note was at 5.12%, unchanged from where it closed Tuesday. The price of precious metals was falling, as was the price of bitcoin, which was recently trading just above $64,000, according to CoinDesk. Oil prices were also slipping. West Texas Intermediate, the U.S. oil price benchmark, was recently down 1% to about $85 a barrel.

Nvidia Results Beat Expectations

Nvidia (NVDA) shares were rising in early trading after the company posted strong results on Tuesday evening and raised its outlook. The chip giant beat expectations on the top and bottom lines, with revenue more than doubling over the past year. Nvidia said it doesn't plan to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and signaled that the drama isn't weighing on its outlook by lifting its fourth-quarter earnings growth rate and revenue projections. Nvidia shares plummeted last week as news spread that Huang reportedly had an affair with a Chinese spy, and fell further when he resigned. The stock was up 3% ahead of today's opening bell.

Investors Await Anthropic IPO Pricing

Anthropic plans to finalize share prices this evening for its IPO, and the numbers may top its initial price range, The Wall Street Journal reported. The AI lab is slated to make its trading debut on the Nasdaq this Thursday, with shares trading under the ticker "ANT." Anthropic previously estimated shares would sell for $70 to $78, which would give the company behind Claude a $1.4 trillion valuation. But strong investor demand could lead Anthropic to lift share prices above $80, which would put its valuation closer to $1.5 or $1.6 trillion, The Journal said.

US stock futures advanced on Wednesday as stronger-than-expected results and an improved revenue outlook from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) supported technology shares, while investors awaited the pricing of Anthropic's (NASDAQ:ANT) initial public offering.

Markets were also assessing expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate increases, declining gold prices and lower crude oil futures amid indications of improving global supplies.

The gains followed Tuesday's declines across Wall Street's three main indices, with technology sector developments remaining a central focus for investors.

Nasdaq Futures Gain 0.9% as Technology Shares Recover

At 04:14 ET (09:14 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures had risen 252 points, or 0.9%, while S&P 500 futures advanced 36 points, or 0.5%.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures increased 103 points, equivalent to 0.2%.

Benchmark US Treasury yields declined, providing additional support to equity markets following recent volatility.

The gains came after Nvidia released its first quarterly results since the departure of former Chief Executive Jensen Huang.

Investors were also preparing for Anthropic's anticipated stock market debut, with the artificial intelligence company expected to price its initial public offering on Wednesday ahead of trading beginning Thursday.

Meanwhile, expectations of further US monetary tightening continued to influence currency and commodity markets.

Gold fell below $3,800 per ounce for the first time in more than a year, while the US dollar index gained more than 0.2%.

Nvidia Raises Quarterly Revenue Guidance to $130 Billion

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) reported third-quarter revenue exceeding $100 billion for the first time, with sales approximately doubling compared with the previous year.

The semiconductor manufacturer also issued current-quarter revenue guidance of $130 billion, exceeding analysts' expectations.

For its next financial year, Nvidia now expects revenue growth of approximately 75%, compared with its previous forecast of 70%.

The results indicated continued demand for artificial intelligence computing infrastructure despite concerns about the scale and profitability of investment across the sector.

Analysts at Stifel said the company's results and increased forecasts provided further evidence of sustained demand for AI infrastructure.

Nvidia shares gained more than 2% in extended trading, although they subsequently reduced some of their earlier advances.

The stock had declined substantially in recent sessions, reaching its lowest level since July 2025 amid uncertainty surrounding the company's leadership and regulatory environment.

title: Oracle Just Dropped 10% in a Month. Executed Perfectly, It’s “a Multiple of Where It Is Today,” per Gil Luria
detail:
Oracle Just Dropped 10% in a Month. Executed Perfectly, It’s “a Multiple of Where It Is Today,” per Gil Luria
Wiltone Asuncion

Oracle Just Dropped 10% in a Month. Executed Perfectly, It's "a Multiple of Where It Is Today," per Gil Luria ©alengo from Getty Images Signature, Ali Raza via Canva
Key Takeaways

Oracle stock is down 10% in the past month, mostly in an AI infrastructure selloff that hit CoreWeave and Nvidia harder.

Days after capping new capital raises at $20 billion through fiscal 2030, Oracle raised all of it, then reportedly dropped a Tencent deal and lost a Microsoft rental contract.

Oracle's plan for positive free cash flow in the second half of fiscal 2028 rests on a $664 billion backlog that leans heavily on OpenAI.

At 14x forward earnings, the stock looks like a buy for investors who can wait until fiscal 2029, and the December quarterly report is the next test.

Oracle (ORCL:NYSE) stock is down 10% in the month through the Nov. 17 close, mostly with the AI trade. The Nasdaq 100 fell 7.5%, and CoreWeave (CRWV:NASDAQ) and Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) fell harder, by 15% and 27%.

All of Oracle's own news came back to one question: can it turn its backlog into cash before the bills come due?

A $20 billion cap, spent in five days

At its Investor Day on Oct. 28, Oracle put a date on the cash. It expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 and to top $30 billion in fiscal 2029, on the way to $21 or more of non-GAAP EPS in fiscal 2030. It also capped new capital raises through fiscal 2030 at $20 billion, not counting refinancing. Analysts expect normalized EPS to more than double by fiscal 2029:

Oracle (ORCL): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (years to May) (TIKR)

Then, Oracle used the whole cap at once. On Nov. 2, it priced 86.2 million new shares at $116 each, right around the stock's Nov. 17 close of $115, and $10 billion of notes. That clears the overhang, but any cost overrun now has to come from customers, vendors or Oracle's own cash.

TIKR tracks 42 analysts on Oracle. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Oracle, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Oracle's Analyst Ratings

Two deals ended, and the AI trade did the rest

The Financial Times reported on Nov. 4 that Oracle had walked away from a chip-leasing deal with Tencent worth about $7 billion after U.S. officials raised concerns. Two days later, Bloomberg reported that Microsoft is letting a 2023 contract to rent older Nvidia chips from Oracle wind down. Neither leaves much of a hole: Tencent's deal was worth about 1% of Oracle's $664 billion backlog, and GPUs up for renewal went at a 20% premium last quarter.

The customer that matters most is OpenAI. Steve Eisman, host of The Real Eisman Playbook podcast, ties about half of that backlog to OpenAI. That's where Nvidia comes in. The Information reported on Nov. 12, the day Colette Kress became Nvidia's interim CEO, that as finance chief she had pushed back on a proposed $250 billion credit backstop for OpenAI. If Nvidia guarantees less of OpenAI's borrowing, OpenAI has to find that money somewhere else to pay Oracle.

CoreWeave pulled the group the other way. On Nov. 10, it beat on its third quarter, raised its full-year guidance and said customer prepayments and contract-backed loans would pay for its buildout. Oracle rose 8.8% with it the next day. CoreWeave also says new contracts are pricing at $20 million to $25 million per megawatt a year, above the roughly $16 million Oracle has cited. Can Oracle's cost-plus deals keep up?

Cheap, if the cash shows up

Oracle trades at 14x forward earnings, against a five-year average of 21x:

Oracle (ORCL): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

D.A. Davidson's managing director and head of technology research, Gil Luria, thinks the upside is big if Oracle delivers. As he put it on the Nov. 16 episode of The Real Eisman Playbook, "If they execute perfectly, the stock is a multiple of where it is today."

The math backs him up. If Oracle hits $21 of non-GAAP EPS in fiscal 2030 and the stock holds today's 14x, that's about $294 a share, more than 2.5x the Nov. 17 close. The $236 consensus target is about double. But perfect is a high bar. Free cash flow slipped below zero in fiscal 2025:

Oracle (ORCL): free cash flow, $ billions, fiscal 2021-2025 (years to May) (TIKR)

In fiscal 2026, it was negative $23.7 billion. Consensus has $17.5 billion for fiscal 2029, not much more than half of Oracle's target.

Bottom line: Oracle's plan still adds up if the backlog turns into cash. That makes the stock look like a buy for investors who can wait until fiscal 2029 and are willing to bet on OpenAI paying until then.

The first test is the fiscal second-quarter report in December. Oracle guided for revenue growth of 30% to 34% and non-GAAP EPS of $1.85 to $1.93. Results inside that range, with the backlog still above $664 billion, would show that losing Tencent and Microsoft didn't leave a hole.

1. Futures rise

U.S. stock futures pointed higher on Wednesday. By 04:14 ET (09:14 GMT), the Nasdaq 100 futures contract had risen by 252 points, or 0.9%, S&P 500 futures had climbed by 36 points, or 0.5%, and Dow futures were up by 103 points, or 0.2%. Benchmark U.S. Treasury yields, which tend to move inversely to prices, declined.

Investors spent much of the prior session awaiting Nvidia's first results since the shock departure of rockstar CEO Jensen Huang last week. All three of the major indices on Wall Street ended in the red on Tuesday.

Hovering in the background was Claude chatbot maker Anthropic's potentially landmark initial public offering, with the stock expected to be priced later today and begin trading on Thursday. Demand for the IPO has soared, media reports have indicated.

At the same time, traders are factoring in the prospect of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes in the coming months, including possibly a quarter-point one in December. Gold, a non-yielding asset whose appeal is dented by elevated rates, slipped below $3,800 an ounce for the first time in more than a year. A tracker of the dollar against a basket of currency pairs gained over 0.2%.

2. Nvidia raises guidance

Is the ship of Nvidia steadying, changing course, or both? Where does this company go without the charismatic leadership of Huang, the only CEO it's ever had?

While those questions remain largely unanswered, Nvidia has continued to deliver the type of blowout earnings that have made the company a lynchpin of the AI boom. Worries have recently abounded over the eventual returns from massive AI infrastructure spending, although, if Nvidia's results are any indication, demand for AI remains robust.

After sales roughly doubled in the third quarter, surging above $100 billion for the first time, the California-based group offered better-than-expected current-quarter revenue guidance of $130 billion. Revenue is also anticipated to grow by 75% in its next fiscal year, up from a previous outlook of 70%.

Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com, notes that Nvidia's third-quarter results provide a strong answer to any concerns that demand for AI infrastructure might be cooling. With fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $130 billion tracking well ahead of estimates, AI infrastructure demand remains incredibly robust, allowing investors to take reassurance from the sheer scale of the beat after the stock's steep decline last week.

However, Hathorn cautions that Huang's departure creates a crucial leadership test while the business is still rapidly expanding. While his exit is unlikely to change already-committed hyperscaler orders, competitors now have an opening to pitch alternatives for future partnerships. Investors will be closely watching whether the next permanent CEO can retain key talent and maintain Nvidia's strategic roadmap to turn today's explosive demand into lasting, sustainable growth.
